list.title: Projects
list.subtitle: Group applications and databases by project.
list.emptyBody: Projects group your apps, databases, and stacks in one place.

create.title: New project
create.description: A project groups the applications and databases you deploy.

empty.applications: No applications in this project yet.
empty.compose: No compose stacks in this project yet.
empty.databases: No databases in this project yet.

detail.counts: {apps, plural, one {# application} other {# applications}} · {stacks, plural, one {# stack} other {# stacks}} · {dbs, plural, one {# database} other {# databases}}

dangerZone.title: Danger zone
dangerZone.deleteDescription: Permanently deletes the project and everything listed in it. This cannot be undone.

resource.empty: No applications, databases or stacks are running in this project.
resource.containerSum: sum of {count, plural, one {# container} other {# containers}}

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can see this project. Platform owners/admins and the project creator are always included; other members are added by the e-mail of an existing account (invite from Settings<arrow></arrow>Team).
members.creator: project creator
members.legend: Admins manage members and can delete the project; developers do everything else; viewers can only read.

export.label: Export configuration (JSON)
export.withoutSecretsHint: Database passwords and environment variables are left blank (passwords are generated anew on import)
export.withSecrets: With database passwords and environment variables
export.withSecretsHint: Keep this file as safe as any other secret

import.title: Import project
import.description: Create a new project from an export file (*.aoox.json). Nothing is deployed; databases are created empty and applications wait for their first deploy.
import.name: Project name (optional)
import.namePlaceholder: Use the name from the file
import.invalidJson: The file is not valid JSON
import.importedWithWarnings: Project imported with {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} — see below.
import.created: Created: {applications} applications, {databases} databases, {composeApps} compose, {domains} domains, {mounts} mounts, {jobs} jobs.

environments.title: Environments
environments.description: Variables shared by this project's applications and stacks, one set per environment. Each application picks one in its Settings.
environments.addDescription: A new, empty set of variables, for example a preview or QA copy.
environments.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 32 characters.
environments.variableCount: {count, plural, =0 {No variables} one {# variable} other {# variables}}
environments.empty: No variables in this environment yet.
environments.revealNote: Showing the values is recorded in the audit log.
environments.viewerNote: Viewers can see variable names only.
environments.protectedNote: Only project admins can reveal or edit the values of {name}.
environments.editorHint: Applications reference these as {ref}. Changes apply on the next deploy.
environments.applyNote: Changes apply to applications and stacks on their next deploy, not to running containers.
environments.deleteItemDescription: The environment and all its variables are deleted permanently, together with its version history. This cannot be undone.
environments.deleteDescription: The variables of this environment are deleted permanently. Nothing is using it.
environments.deleteInUse: Still used by {apps}. Switch them to another environment first.
environments.secretNote: Secret variables are always masked in deployment logs.

history.title: History of {name}
history.description: Every change to the variables of this environment. Values are never shown here.
history.empty: No changes recorded yet. The first change creates a version.

action.baseline: Content before the first recorded change

history.restoreBody: {name} gets the variables it had on {when}. This is saved as a new version, so nothing is lost and you can undo it from this history.
history.viewerNote: Viewers can read the history but not restore versions.
history.protectedNote: Only project admins can restore versions of {name}.

compare.title: Compare environments
compare.description: Compare two environments variable by variable. Only names are shown, never values.
compare.sameCount: {count, plural, =0 {No variable has the same value on both sides} one {# variable is the same on both sides} other {# variables are the same on both sides}}
compare.notComparable: Values are not compared because you cannot read both environments. Only names that exist on one side are shown, and nothing can be promoted.
compare.confirmBody: These variables are copied from {from} into {to}. A variable that already exists in {to} gets the new value; comments and order in {to} are kept, and new variables are added at the end. This is saved as a new version.
compare.promoted: {count, plural, one {# variable promoted} other {# variables promoted}} to {name}
compare.nothing: Nothing differs that could be promoted.
